The lie is real, it REACHES the guest, the guest DOES read the field -- and on the shipping value no guest on any rig is harmed. Priority drops; the fix does not become unnecessary. *** * TRAFFIC: pmax/OpenBSD 2.2 (old-style rz driver) issues ZERO MODE SENSE across a full multiuser boot plus disklabel, mount and raw dd -- a clean negative. arc/OpenBSD 2.2 issues 5x MODE SENSE(6) page 4: asked 32, got 32, TOLD 132, true 36. That reproduces the brief's capture exactly. luna88k/OpenBSD 7.7 issues 11x across pages 0/4/8: asked 254, got 254, TOLD 98. * *** THE WRAP IS ALREADY EXERCISED IN NORMAL OPERATION: luna88k asks 254, so 254+100=354 WRAPS to 98. *** It merely lands on a value the guest tolerates. Measured sweep: reported==0 at exactly alloc==156, and reported < true-1 for alloc in [156,190]. No rig asks 156, so the defect is ONE allocation-length change away from the arm-C behaviour below, not a hypothetical. * THE CHANNEL IS LIVE, proved by a POSITIVE CONTROL rather than assumed: sending cyl=1234/heads=9 changes arc's attach line from '2081 cyl, 16 head, 63 sec' to '1234 cyl, 9 head, 188 sec'. The response body IS consumed. * AND IT REFUTED ITS OWN DRAFT: it had written that a page-4 rpm change proves consumption; arm D showed disklabel still printed 3600 because that value comes from the ON-DISK LABEL, not from MODE SENSE. The control killed its own claim before it shipped. * HARM, MEASURED: luna88k told-98 vs told-35/11 produce ORDERED TRANSCRIPTS IDENTICAL, 0 diff lines across 97 lines each. But told-0 FLIPS CONTROL FLOW -- 32 MODE SENSE instead of 11, including MODE SENSE(10) fallbacks and page 5. OpenBSD 7.7 branches on this byte. So 98 and 132 sit in a tolerated 'nonzero and >= true' region; 0 does not. * *** THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG: `retlen -= 100` writes the ALLOCATION LENGTH. *** The spec wants true_len-1, measured as 11/23/35/35/43 for pages 0/1/3/4/5 -- the allocation length is correct only by coincidence at alloc==191. The true value is not known at :607 because the page is written later at :630+, so the write must MOVE AFTER the pagecode switch. * BLAST RADIUS: nothing reads retlen after :607 (next use :746 is an assignment in the READ case), and data_in[0] is read NOWHERE outside diskimage_scsicmd.c across all of src/ -- every HBA sizes from data_in_len, so the guest is the only consumer. No overflow: max write is q+29 = 45 against a >=100-byte buffer. * DETECTOR built and feasible offline. TWO DESIGN POINTS THAT MATTER: the rows MUST SPAN PAGES {0,1,3,4,5}, because every page-4 case has true_len 36 and a mutant hardcoding 35 would pass a page-4-only test; and an INVARIANCE row -- the reported length must not vary with the allocation length -- NAMES THE DEFECT RATHER THAN A VALUE, so a '+100 -> +0' half-fix cannot pass it. -ffunction-sections/-Wl,--gc-sections is required or mymkstemp/debug_indentation fail to link. * ADJACENT, measured en route: MODE SENSE(10) writes the 6-BYTE header layout, so a conformant guest parses block_desc_len=0 while 8 real descriptor bytes sit at offset 8 -- STRICTLY WORSE than b120r, and unreached today only because no rig issues MS10. And data_in_len is set to the FULL allocation length even when far less data exists (alloc 255 -> 255 bytes, 219 of them zeros) where a real drive transfers 36, which affects residual logic. * HONEST UNKNOWN, stated by the seat: three guests measured, ALL OpenBSD. Whether a NetBSD/Ultrix/Linux driver asks an allocation length in [156,190] was not measured. * It also caught a citation error of mine: REQUEST SENSE forcing is :964-967, not the :957-960 my brief claimed. gateflrgateflr If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it noticesgateflr If a whole gate block is deleted, nothing outside it notices — HOLD: FILE: measured during the R1+R2 regression review — Found by the flagship while reviewing the R1 and R2 regression evidence. The new gate-2 block guards itself: its floors, its named-row greps and its positive control are all INSIDE the block. Delete the block and every one of those guards disappears with it, while the gate still reports PASS - nothing outside floors gate 2's check count. This is the vacuity class in a new place: not a row that cannot fail, but a whole section that can be removed silently. A committed per-gate check-count floor, asserted by the runner rather than by the gate, is the shape of the fix.held

hlenhlen Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit)hlen Device handlers that ignore the access length (audit) — HOLD: census done; promote to a FIX round? — Opened from the b75 refutation, then characterized by census. A device handler that switches on the address and cannot service a width will read or write only the first register of an 8-byte access. MEASURED SCOPE: 62 spanning-capable handlers of 167 registered; 20 on machines this project boots. TWO BOOTED MACHINES ARE PROVABLY IMMUNE - SH-4 has no 8-byte access at all (fmov.d is two 4-byte accesses) and MIPS32/R3000A treats LD/SD as reserved, so landisk and pmax cannot produce the access. NO CONVENTION EXISTS in the tree: no helper, no macro, no rule - only three hand-rolled decompositions that are all big-endian-specific and that disagree with each other about the else branch, so there is no single idiom to copy. FIRST WITNESS NAMED: dev_irqc on testarm, the only spanning-capable device on that machine, where the two halves of one aligned 8-byte access have OPPOSITE legal directions (status is read-only, mask is write-only), which makes the miss unambiguous. DETECTOR SHAPE: an offline differential in the diff_*.c family - no boot, no rig, no serialization.held

Three binaries in a private tree: * HEAD scores 9/15 rows against the architecture; MASK AT THE ACCESS scores 15/15; MASK AT ENTRY scores 14/15 and CORRUPTS THE BASE WRITEBACK (0x00070004 for 0x00070006). *** #357's 'mask at entry corrupts the writeback' is REAL, NOT FOLKLORE -- the mutant was built and measured. *** * The divergence, three ways: the SAME LDM run twice against one page returns 0x77881122 then 0x11223344; ONE LDM WITH TWO REGISTERS returns r1 from a raw unaligned address and r3 from an aligned one -- MIXED WITHIN A SINGLE INSTRUCTION, because r1's own access warmed the page; and a cold STM SPILLS INTO THE NEXT WORD (0x00FF3344 / 0x5566FFFF). * IT SIDESTEPPED THE `put w` WARMS / `put b` DOES NOT TRAP RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT: the slow path's own memory_rw inserts the page on its way out (memory_rw.c:732, no NO_EXCEPTIONS), so the first bdt access to a cold page is slow and every later one is fast. Running the IDENTICAL instruction twice makes the divergence a difference between two executions rather than a value that depends on trusting a seeding rule. * FIX: two lines, cpu_arm_instr.c:1563 (load) and :1752 (store), addr -> addr & ~(uint32_t)3. Confirmed from the CODE (`uint32_t addr = *np` at :1514, `if (w_bit) *np = addr` at :1624 -- addr IS the writeback value), from the LOCAL manual (A5.4.2 p.A5-43; LDM(1) p.A4-37, STM(1) p.A4-190), and from the ENTRY mutant. NUANCE it caught: the Multi-word row of Table A2-10 is on the CONTINUATION page A2-41, not A2-40 where the table starts. * IN-TREE PRECEDENT it did not expect: generate_arm_multi.c:117 already emits `addr &= 0xffc` and the generated combiners write back from the UNMASKED register -- upstream's own generated LDM combiners already use exactly this shape, and they fall back to instr(bdt_load) on a cold page, so they inherit both the defect and the fix. Thumb PUSH/POP (cpu_arm.c:1670,1677) call the same two functions; arm_pop/arm_push have exactly four callers, all enumerated. * *** THE EXISTING GATE IS BLIND TO IT, MEASURED: arm_writeback_probe.py scores 22/22 on ALL THREE binaries including the ENTRY mutant that corrupts the writeback, and gate 14's 261 checks touch neither arm_pop nor arm_push. *** The single check separating the correct fix from the #357 trap is the W=1 writeback row. So the gate row is NOT redundant and must land in the SAME commit as the fix, being scored against architecture rather than against HEAD. * Side effect named rather than left to be found: masking also removes the 4 KB page-straddle path for bdt, where a raw access at P+0xFFE currently translates once and takes its tail from the physical continuation. * It also caught a records defect against the main loop: _scratchpad/CHECKPOINT.md had gone stale, naming HEAD 4d0981d and 'Tree CLEAN' when HEAD was 9bcae1c and two files were uncommitted. Research (fix proposals)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** REPRODUCED AT RUNG 3 -- AND THREE OF THIS ROW'S CLAIMS ARE MEASURED FALSE. *** The defect is real; the severity argument that put it top of a cluster is not. THE WITNESS: unmodified in-tree `testppc` (-E testppc -C PPC750 -M 32), cold debugger, real guest instructions, real decode, real memory_rw. A PPC guest sets DBAT0 over a 128 KB window, sets MSR[DR]=1, and executes `stw r6,0(r5)` with r5 = 0x1201fffe -- unaligned, crossing the 1 KB split granule. Head (2 bytes) reaches the in-tree `fb` device; tail (2 bytes) has no BAT and no PTE, so a real DSI fires; a planted `rfi` at the DSI vector is the GUEST'S OWN restart. The same instruction re-executes, unbounded. Counters: one architectural store, FOUR device writes. **The trace is from a fully stock HEAD binary with zero instrumentation** -- the counters only counted. Controls all green: liveness (RAM through the same decode), DEVICE SIGNATURE (same program, only DBAT0L changed: PA->device reads back 0x3344, PA->no device reads back 0x0000), and a negative control two bytes lower that does not split. CLAIM 1 -- 'not introduced by #430' -- MEASURED FALSE. Built from `git show 2458cfb^:src/cpus/memory_rw.c`, stock otherwise: the same guest program produces NO exception, NO restart, ONE device write. Pre-#430 the tail was silently mis-applied to the physically-following location -- the defect #430 fixed -- so there was nothing to restart. **#430 CREATED the fault, and the double-application is a direct consequence of it.** CLAIM 2 -- 'the memblock split has had this property all along' -- MEASURED FALSE, twice. Post-#430 the memblock split can only fire on PHYSICAL accesses (a translated 4 KB write across 1 MB costs 4 translations / 4 host lookups; PHYSICAL costs 0 / 2), and its head can NEVER be a device in either version because device dispatch `goto do_return_ok`s first -- measured with a device straddling the memblock boundary. CLAIM 3 -- '256x' -- MEASURED WRONG: it is **1024x**. The granule was measured by walking offsets, not read: MRW_SPLIT_MASK is 0x3ff, so 1 MB / 1024 = 1024. The 256 came from comparing 1 MB to a 4 KB page -- the granule this split does not use. *** THE SAME WRONG NUMBER WAS ALSO IN THE SOURCE, at memory_rw.c's own 'one boundary in 256' comment: ONE mis-derived constant became TWO records defects, and the row repeated it as a severity argument. Both corrected. *** REACHABILITY IS FAR NARROWER THAN THE ROW IMPLIES, and this is why it re-ranks DOWN: * ONLY PowerPC can emit a straddling store at all. MIPS (AdES; swl/swr do an ALIGNED RMW), ARM, SH, M88K and Alpha all force alignment -- each checked in source. PPC's `if (addr & (LS_SIZE-1))` at cpu_ppc_instr_loadstore.c:229 is a FAST-PATH BAIL-OUT, not an exception, so the generic path passes the unaligned address through. * PPC is also the ONLY family whose device-failure path can restart: memory_rw's device-failure arm raises an exception only under #ifdef MEM_MIPS / #ifdef MEM_M88K. * THREE REAL GUEST BOOTS, instrumented: OpenBSD/pmax to root login, OpenBSD/luna88k to `login:`, NetBSD/macppc to the root-device prompt -- **ZERO straddling stores from guest code**. The seat first read macppc's 95 split-loop writes as guest activity and REFUTED ITSELF by logging the addresses: all are len=65536 at pc=0x0, i.e. file_elf.c:448's loader chunks running before any guest instruction. * Of the 1024 offsets in a granule only ELEVEN (0x3f9..0x3ff) can start a straddling 2/4/8-byte access, and the head's device offset is always within 7 bytes BELOW a 1 KB boundary -- so a register at offset 0x00/0x10/0x20 can never be a straddle head. *** AND THE FIX MAY ITSELF BE WRONG. *** Partial completion on a page-crossing misaligned store, with restart re-applying the first part, is what real PowerPC hardware does -- so gxemul may be CORRECT here and a fix may introduce a divergence. There is no PowerPC manual in _scratchpad/ (ARM, MIPS and m88k only), so the seat stated that as REASONING, NOT A CITATION -- the same trap CLAUDE.md records for SH. **Obtain a PPC manual before any edit.** The minimal fix, if one is wanted: a dry-run pre-pass on WRITES only, walking the chunks with FLAG_NOEXCEPTIONS and committing only if all translate. Zero cost on the hot path -- it sits inside the `while (len > granule - offset)` body, which no aligned access enters. Watch TLB-miss handlers with side effects (PPC603 software reload) and do not let the dry run update referenced/changed bits. mrwstore2_rung3.py is close to shippable as a regress detector; its controls already satisfy the liveness and device-signature clauses. — evidence: _scratchpad/ (mrwstore2_rung3.py, sig.py, probe_mrwstore2.c)·······

Four defects are now specifiable. (1) SS7.3.41 bit 6: FREERUN wraps to FFFFFFh and keeps counting; PERIODIC reloads TimerNLoad; the clock source is bits 3:2 alone, identical in both. reload_timer_value() computes one rate and hands it to a repeating timer -- the PERIODIC cadence unconditionally -- so a FREERUN timer is too fast by up to 2^24/load. (2) TimerNValue is READ-ONLY (SS7.3.38/7.3.40) but the model accepts a guest write, and TIMER_1_CLEAR has NO writeflag test, so a guest READ of a write-only register reloads the counter and deasserts the IRQ. (3) Reset values diverge: hardware gives CONTROL 0x00 and LOAD 0, the model gives TIMER_MODE_PERIODIC and TIMER_MAX_VAL -- and this is the model bug #432's first draft mistakenly cited as evidence for its own zero mapping. (4) The random() counter model is now fully specified by SS7.3.40 + SS7.3.41 bit 7: a 24-bit down-counter, readable any time, RETAINED across disable and resuming on re-enable. The author's TODO is discharged; only a rig is missing. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260815_221232/✓2026-08-16 — MANUAL — Expand the item: external-event handling, reserved CONTROL-bit masking, and the retained/down-counter model belong in it alongside the four already listed. Research (fix proposals)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** REPRODUCED AT RUNG 3, AND MY OWN PREMISE FOR THE TASK WAS WRONG. *** I briefed the measure seat that NO rig reaches the 8253 -- only algor/cobalt/evbmips/iyonix via bus_isa -- and that a rung-4 witness therefore almost certainly did not exist. HALF FALSE, and the false half is what made rung 3 reachable. `bus_isa_init` has SIX callers outside src/machines/: bus_pci.c:476 and :1060, dev_eagle.c:160,172, dev_lca.c:376, dev_prep.c:80. My grep looked only at src/machines/ and bus_*.c and I reported the subset as the whole. **cats** reaches the 8253 through machine_cats.c -> dev_footbridge.c:730 (bus_pci_add "ali_m1543") -> bus_pci.c:459/476, at isa_portbase 0x7c000000. Verified here independently. THE WITNESS: a cold-debugger probe on UNMODIFIED `-E cats`, the same mechanics as footbridge_sites_probe.py. Pre-fix and post-fix binaries from the same tree, same script: C1 liveness 0x11223344 both RAM through the same decode A1 device signature 0xAA both see below T1 negative control halts at paddr=0x0c000043, MMU-on cannot reach it D0 count 0 -> hz 0 Hz -> 18 Hz the device's own report G0 guest-visible IRR 0x0 -> 0x1 after a 1.9 s free-run D1 positive control count 4608 -> 259 Hz, IRR=0x1, identical both ways All four controls green in BOTH runs; only the two symptom rows move. THE DEVICE SIGNATURE IS A VALUE RAM CANNOT PRODUCE, and it was designed against the exact trap that ate the footbridge probe's first draft. The guest writes 0xAA then 0x55 to the SAME address in 16-bit mode, writes the MODE register (a different address), then reads back and gets 0xAA -- the byte from two writes ago. RAM returns 0x55. Nonzero deliberately, because 0x0 is what an ABSENT device looks like. TWO CAVEATS THE SEAT OWNED RATHER THAN HID: G0/G1 use a WALL-CLOCK window (1.9 s against a 55 ms correct period, ~34 chances), which is why the post-fix green is the settlement and not the window size; and its first T1 draft reported FAIL through a string-equality bug in its own script, which it found and fixed. All 27 instruction encodings were checked against the emulator's own disassembler before use -- the hand-assembled-encoding trap this project has hit four times. REACHABILITY, MEASURED: no guest in this tree programs count 0. Every PIT write in _guest-src-openbsd22/sys/ is TIMER_DIV(x) (never 0) or 0xff/0xff, and no rig image boots an 8253 machine. A recollection that Linux's pit_shutdown() writes 0,0 was flagged RECALLED, UNVERIFIED rather than cited -- the right handling. *** BUT FINDING `pitflip` BELOW MANUFACTURES COUNT 0 FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER ASKS FOR IT, which changes the reachability picture entirely. *** MAPPINGS, measured not read: cats and netwinder 0x7c000040; malta/maltabe 0x18000040; cobalt 0x10000040; iyonix 0x90000040; absent on prep, mvmeppc, algor, arc. THE FIX is one line -- hz = (int)(I8253_TIMER_FREQ / 65536.0 + 0.5) -> 18 -- and d->hz[] is read only at :133/137/140, all inside the MSB arm, so the blast radius is that arm. *** DO NOT GENERALISE BY ANALOGY: dev_rtc.c:129 and dev_mc146818.c:409 look identical and are CORRECT -- for those devices zero genuinely means 'off', and dev_rtc.c's comment records a prior round reasoning that through. The 8254 is the opposite case. *** Minor: int hz[3] rounds 18.2065 to 18 (-1.1%) while timer_add takes a double. — evidence: _scratchpad/t8253/ (pit8253_count0_probe.py, pit8253_site_probe.py)·······

Same device, one oracle (the device's own `[ 8253: counter %i set to %i (%i Hz) ]`), and ONE restructure fixes both: hoist the recompute + timer_add/timer_update_frequency into a helper called under a 'load complete per programmed format' predicate, with count == 0 => 65536. *** THE SEQUENCING IS NOW FORCED, which is information the cluster panel did not have: *** #440 introduces wr_msb[3], a per-counter write flip-flop. That IS the completeness predicate the merged fix needs. Designing this before #440 would have had to invent it; after #440 it is free. A TRAP TO WRITE INTO THE BRIEF: do NOT simply recompute in both arms. In 16-bit format the LSB half must NOT recompute, because `counter` then holds (stale_high | new_low) -- that would call timer_update_frequency with a garbage rate, re-introducing precisely the transient-wrong-hz that pitflip was filed for. *** AND THIS ROW'S WITNESS IS NOT RE-RUNNABLE. *** 1ce189c ('i8253zero REPRODUCED at rung 3') changed tools/pipeline/ledger.json ONLY -- no probe script -- and the row's witness field is None. That rung-3 result exists as a transcript. Before the merged round ships, its D0-equivalent row must exist AS A FILE, or the fix lands with a witness nobody can reproduce: the fifth vacuity class in its hardest-to-see shape, because a transcript LOOKS like evidence. Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** DO NOT DROP, DO NOT FIX AS WRITTEN -- THE FILED FIX IS PROVABLY INERT, AND THE REAL ITEM IS BIGGER. *** Two seats dropped this for being READ-only and the adjudicator overturned on mechanism; both were reasoning about the wrong fix. MEASURED (build/gxemul, -v -v -V -T -E cats -M 32): device order is 8259 @0x7c000020, 8259 @0x7c0000a0, *** 8253 @0x7c000040 ADDED AFTER BOTH PICs, *** pccmos @0x7c000070. The pointer copy sits at bus_isa.c:224-225, between the first device_add (:223) and the second (:235); the 8253's device_add is at :244. Construction order confirmed in the RUNNING PROGRAM, not inferred -- and it independently confirms the 0x7c000040 mapping. MEASURED (grep census): pending_timer_interrupts has exactly ONE writer (dev_8253.c:282) and TWO pointer-cachers (bus_isa.c:225, dev_v3.c:298), both caching before their 8253 can exist. *** MEASURED, AND THIS IS THE PART NOBODY STATED: dev_8253.c contains ZERO decrements of pending_interrupts_timer0. *** Every other timer device in the tree drains its own counter from inside its own DEVICE_ACCESS handler -- dev_jazz.c:423,443, dev_luna88k.c:800, dev_mc146818.c:563, dev_vr41xx.c:634, dev_footbridge.c:583,594-595. The 8253 ALONE outsourced its drain to bus_isa.c:134-138. READ: that drain is unreachable for TWO INDEPENDENT reasons, *** so moving the pointer copy after device_add -- the fix as filed -- changes NOTHING observable: *** (1) nothing ever calls isa_interrupt_deassert for line 0, as dev_8253.c has no INTERRUPT_DEASSERT; and (2) dev_8259.c clears irr DIRECTLY on EOI (:107, :122), bypassing the isa deassert handler entirely. REFILE AS: 'the 8253's pending-interrupt counter has no reachable drain -- it is the only timer device in the tree that cannot ack', grade DESIGN + needs-witness. Consequence (READ): once any guest touches the PIT, in_use goes 1, the counter rises monotonically and never drains, so DEVICE_TICK re-asserts isa.0 on EVERY device tick (TICK_SHIFT 14) rather than at the programmed rate. TWO THINGS THE FILING SEAT MISSED: dev_v3.c:298 is not merely 'the same shape' -- it is the same bug for the same reason needing the same two-part fix; and if a machine ever created two ISA buses (bus_pci.c calls bus_isa_init at :476 and :1060), the second copy would be NON-NULL AND ALIAS THE FIRST BUS'S 8253 -- worse than NULL, and silent. THE WITNESS THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, rung 3 on -E cats: program counter 0 to ~18 Hz, free-run 200 ms, read the 8259 IRR (expect bit0), write specific-EOI 0x60 to 0x7c000020, free-run ~5 ms, read IRR again. Draining correctly => 0 (next tick due at ~55 ms); no drain => 1 again on the very next device tick. Clean discriminator, no source change. — evidence: build/gxemul -E cats device order; grep census of the drain sites·······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** THE SMALLEST EDIT THAT BREAKS #429 AND SURVIVES ITS ENTIRE TABLE. *** MEASURED. src/devices/dev_rtc.c:92 idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, len); -> idata = memory_readmax64(cpu, data, 4); On a little-endian guest a 2^32 write yields idata = 0 -> d->hz = 0 -> *** THE ADD BECOMES A REMOVE, *** the exact mechanism diff_rtc_range.c's own header describes. Result: 18 rows, 0 failures, RTC_RANGE_PASS. Invisible because the STUB returns stub_in whole and never looks at len. #427's clamp in timer.c cannot mask it -- the timer is GONE, not clamped. It came out of a full census over the HZ write path (18 statement deletions + 12 substitutions) which found TEN survivors. The other nine worth naming: `>` -> `>=` (see [[rtcbranch]]); deleting `if (d->timer != NULL)` (:141); deleting `d->timer = NULL` (:144); deleting `d->pending_interrupts = 0` (:145); deleting the `else` at :151; `idata == 0` -> `idata == 1` (a guest asking 1 Hz gets the timer REMOVED -- the 'zero keeps its meaning' rows do not pin that ONLY zero stops it); the 32-bit mask on the pass-through (a true no-op, correct to pass); and timer_add / timer_update_frequency fed raw idata. THREE STUBS ARE UNFAITHFUL AND EACH HIDES A SURVIVOR: memory_readmax64 ignores len AND cpu (the real one dereferences cpu->byte_order and reads exactly len bytes); timer_remove accepts NULL silently, where the real one (timer.c:155-175) walks to cur == NULL, finds `cur == t` TRUE, then dereferences cur->next -- *** a guaranteed NULL deref that the table survives because no row writes 0 with d.timer == NULL, the ordinary reset path; *** and memory_writemax64 is a no-op with no row doing a MEM_READ, so the guest readback (dev_rtc.c:110) is asserted nowhere. fatal is faithful in the respect that matters -- debugmsg.c:384 calls va_debug and does not exit -- so pass 3's 'REFUTED BY SOURCE' record is correct. — evidence: dev_rtc.c:92 one-token mutant, 18 rows green·······

The seats were clear that...". *** Three of those seats had ARGUED IN THEIR OWN FILES THAT ROUND B WAS TOO NARROW, *** and deepseek's 5.3 KB answer never mentions the 0xF5 opcode at issue at all -- yet the record shows five seats concurring with the narrow scope. A harvest that stamps one summary across every seat cell does not merely lose detail: *** it converts 'six seats answered' into 'six seats agreed', which is the exact claim the panel exists to earn. *** It is the seat-count analogue of the padded-column grep trap -- the number looks right and means nothing. *** AND THE FIRST CHECK I WROTE TO VERIFY THE CLAIM REPORTED GREEN. *** It hashed the note text, so a four-character seat-name prefix turned five identical paragraphs into five distinct hashes, and I briefly recorded the seat's finding as measured false. Blindness reported as a green line, in the verification of a finding about blindness being reported as a green line. The shipped check strips the seat's own name before comparing, which is what makes it work. SCALE, measured: 57 clusters across 52 rows, at >= 3 seats sharing a >= 80-char note. That is essentially every cluster panel ever recorded. So the check is FORWARD-ONLY BY DATE, not by an allowlist -- a per-row allowlist at that scale is the check switched off with extra steps, and a rule that retro-fails the archive gets disabled. Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** THE ANSWER TO 'WHAT IS THE SMALLEST EDIT THAT BREAKS THIS AND STILL PASSES', AND IT INVALIDATES THE DETECTOR DESIGN THE wdcnoirq ROUND WAS ABOUT TO SHIP. *** MEASURED, both oracles built in one harness. M1: delete `INTERRUPT_ASSERT(d->irq);` from dev_wdc_tick() (dev_wdc.c:113). ONE LINE. ORACLE A (reads d->int_assert) ORACLE B (counts real asserts) IDENTIFY 0xec int_assert=1 irq_asserts=0 RECAL 0x10 int_assert=1 irq_asserts=0 STANDBY 0xe0 int_assert=1 irq_asserts=0 HELD-LINE 0x10, 1000 ticks: 0 asserts *** Oracle A is 100% green on a controller that can never raise an interrupt, on any machine, for any opcode. *** The detector's oracle for wdcnoirq is THE WRONG VARIABLE. This is diff_wdc_identify.c's own recorded blind spot one level up ('this driver reads identify_struct DIRECTLY rather than through the path the guest uses'). So the wdcnoirq round's detector must count real INTERRUPT_ASSERT calls through d->irq.interrupt_assert, not read d->int_assert. ~6 lines of harness, not a new gate. TWO MORE SURVIVORS FROM THE SAME CENSUS: M3 -- move `d->int_assert = 1;` into wdc_command()'s prologue. Every abort row flips to irq=1 exactly like the real fix, AND *** 0xA0 ATAPI_PKT_CMD flips 0 -> 1, silently re-enabling the interrupt the shipping code DELIBERATELY suppresses at :559 *** (`/* d->int_assert = 1; */`). A 9-row set without an 0xA0 row passes completely. Dangerous because it looks like a tidy-up a later refactor would make. The detector needs an 0xA0 row asserting irq == 0 -- 0xA0 is the file's ONLY deliberate no-interrupt arm and nothing pins it. M4 -- add `d->warned_unimpl = 0;` to the prologue (the flood latch never latches). Flood back to 100/100, and *** every per-opcode row is byte-identical to the correct post-fix build. *** Only a repeat-the-same-opcode-ON-THE-SAME-STRUCT row catches it -- so if the detector allocates a fresh wdc_data per row, which is the natural way to write it, THE FLOOD FIX IS UNDETECTABLE. — evidence: /tmp/opuswdc/probe.c: Oracle A vs Oracle B, M1/M3/M4·······

If rd_msb is already 1 when the latch command arrives, the FIRST latched read has rw == MSB and #440 immediately clears the latch -- so only ONE byte has been read after the count was latched. *** A byte read BEFORE the latch command cannot be a byte of the newly latched value, *** which sits badly with p. 8's 'two bytes must be read'. On that reading R9 pins the implementation's assumption rather than the specification. THE MEASURING SEAT REACHED THE SAME FACT AND THE OPPOSITE READING: at odd parity the first read takes the byte the format calls for and unlatches, which it argues is CLOSER to hardware, and it measured the values (0x9c00 where #439 gave 0x0000). *** BOTH SEATS AGREE ON WHAT THEY CANNOT SETTLE: the local i8254 text does not say whether a Counter Latch Command rewinds the read flip-flop, and there is no other 8253/8254 source in the tree. *** So this is filed as an UNKNOWN and recorded in the source as one, rather than resolved 7-1. An honest UNKNOWN outranks a confident guess, and a majority has been wrong on mechanism in this project at least six times. Codex's proposed shape if it is ever settled against #440: track TWO POST-LATCH READS rather than reusing the format flip-flop -- a boolean `latched` is insufficient when the read phase can be MSB at latch time. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260820_183311/ (7/7 scriptable) + opus5 measuring seat······

Assessment (initial problem)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — Found by the pass-2 measuring seat, and it is a fair hit on the round's own reasoning. PCR/RTCSR/RTCOR/RFCR all do `idata & mask` with NO byte_order term, so on big-endian a 4-byte access to them takes the LAST two bytes while BCR2/BCR3 now take the FIRST; and they PROMOTE a 1-byte write while BCR2/BCR3 now DROP it. The #441 comment cites them to justify servicing and then services differently on both axes. WHICH CONVENTION IS RIGHT IS NOT DECIDABLE HERE: there is no SH-4 document in this tree (sh4_manual.txt is ONE BYTE), so this is an honest UNKNOWN about the hardware and a real internal inconsistency about the model. One round takes one site, so #441 recorded the divergence in the source rather than silently unifying five registers on a guess. A related nit worth carrying: the round's claim that 'BCR1 already consults byte_order' is true but weak precedent -- BCR1 ORs in a strap bit, it does not place a lane. — evidence: pass-2 seat, read against dev_sh4.c·······

I wrote that dfreq ranks last because the footbridge has 'no witness of either kind -- no bootable rig instantiates an ISA bus or a footbridge, AND NO PROBE EXERCISES IT EITHER'. The first clause holds; the second is false and it built the counterexample in one session. `cats` constructs from the same four-byte stub gate_arm.sh uses for testarm, reaches the cold debugger, and `device list` reports a live footbridge AND a full ISA bus (8259, 8253, pckbc, ns16550, vga_ctrl, dec21143, mc146818). A real guest ldr/str then reaches it: TIMER_1_LOAD <- 0x12345678 reads back 0x345678, and THE VANISHING TOP BYTE IS THE HANDLER'S OWN SIGNATURE (dev_footbridge.c:548 stores idata & TIMER_MAX_VAL) -- RAM would have returned it unchanged. So dfreq does not rank last under the new rule; it moves UP. * NEAR-MISS WORTH KEEPING: its first attempt returned 0x0 on every footbridge row WITH THE CONTROL STILL GREEN, because machine_cats.c:131 maps only the low 256 MB and the footbridge sits at PA 0x42000000 -- unreachable until the guest turns the MMU off itself. That run would have 'confirmed' the brief. * AND IT WITNESSED A SECOND exitsweep SITE, killing the stated reason for that round's one-site scope: dev_footbridge.c:495-497, `case IRQ_ENABLE_SET:` on a READ does odata = irq_enable, fatal(), exit(1). Two arms of one script differing by ONE INSTRUCTION -- isolation arm survives with both controls green, kill arm exits 1 with the WARNING text. VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY at those lines. The table row 'reproducible by BOOTING a rig we have -- ONE' is correct as written, but it is NOT the same claim as 'reproducible -- ONE', and it has been read as the second. Seven more footbridge sites sit in the same 0x400 window. * *** THE PROPOSED ANTI-LAUNDERING CLAUSE REJECTS THE PROJECT'S OWN EXEMPLAR. *** regress/m8820x_sites_probe.py states the panel's governing principle VERBATIM and is where the principle comes from -- yet it shipped as 9494c6a, THREE COMMITS AFTER the #433 fix 66b0367 (verified), with every row SURVIVED, post-fix only. It satisfies neither clause (1) 'defect symptom on the pre-fix HEAD' nor clause (2) 'pre-fix failure and post-fix success'. The principle was lifted out of a DETECTOR and is being written as a rule for WITNESSES. * SO THE DETECTOR/WITNESS DISTINCTION IS NOT NEW -- it is committed, in that file's own comment, together with its cost argument (3.2 s cold-debugger vs 182-233 s for a rig drive, ~60x cheaper). Where the project conflates them is not in its ENGINEERING but in its RECORDS: round prose says 'reproduced' without naming the artefact. * A MISSING RUNG, and it names where laundering will actually happen: the real ladder is (1) #include harness -- behaviour only, rejected; (2) MACHINE CONSTRUCTION -- device registered in the address map, no guest instruction, WHICH THE RULE IS SILENT ABOUT and gate 9 already does for every machine type; (3) cold-debugger probe -- real instruction, real decode; (4) boot -- a real driver reaches it unaided. * DROP 'EQUAL': a probe proves a path CAN be reached (right for a bounds fix); a boot proves it IS travelled (right for RANKING). #437 is the illustration -- its luna88k boot showed SYNCHRONIZE CACHE is issued once per boot right after MARKING FILE SYSTEM CLEAN, which no probe could produce. Admissible-equal, subordinate for prioritisation. * RETROACTIVE COST: ZERO closed rows are invalidated (85 rows, 16 closed, scanned). But the check is weaker than it looks and THE REAL FINDING IS A SCHEMA GAP -- the ledger has no field naming WHICH ARTEFACT WITNESSED THE DEFECT, so the question is answerable only by reading prose. b47/#47 is the closest call: its defect witness is the #include differential ('15 of 23 red against the pre-change file') and its boots are no-regression checks, not defect witnesses. * STUBBING DEMONSTRABLY DISTORTS: m8820x's offline reproduction reported 1013/1015/11 where the true numbers are 1007/1009/17 -- a stub artefact, because the harness left invalidate_translation_caches NULL and that callback fires on reads too. The one round that reproduced offline got its numbers wrong, in the direction the principle predicts. * AGREES exitsweep stays at ONE SITE, but on a different and stronger ground: not 'only one is reproducible' (false) but the THIRD DOCTRINE ARM, which bounds it on SEMANTICS and does not evaporate when someone writes a probe. Proposed reopening rule: add a second site only when it is witnessed, in the SAME DEVICE and SAME SEMANTIC CLASS so one fix design covers both, and covered by the SAME DETECTOR without a new oracle -- under which the eight footbridge sites are ONE candidate round, not eight. Research (fix proposals)·…2026-08-19 — *** THE BRIEF'S FRAMING WAS HALF WRONG, AND THE HALF IT GOT WRONG CHANGES WHAT SHOULD BE FIXED. *** Verdict FIX-not-document, but not for the reason I gave it. * 0xE7 WDCC_FLUSHCACHE is DEFINED at wdcreg.h:130 and NEVER REFERENCED in dev_wdc.c; 0xEA has no constant anywhere in src/. Both fall to wdc_command()'s default:, which sets WDCE_ABRT, emits an UNLATCHED fatal(), and -- the part that matters -- does NOT set d->int_assert. MEASURED offline against the shipping wdc_command(): 0xE7 -> err=0x04 irq=0 fatal=1, status 0x51 (DRDY|DSC|ERR), against the 0x10 RECAL control at err=0x00 irq=1. * NO REAL GUEST ISSUES IT, and the negative is WELL CONTROLLED. With an IDE disk attached and a full filesystem lifecycle (MAKEDEV, fdisk, disklabel, newfs 64 MB FFS, mount, write, sync, umount, halt -p) OpenBSD 7.6 issues exactly: 0xEC 0xF5 0x10 0x91 0xC6 0x20 0xC4 0x30 0xC5 0xE0. No 0xE7, no 0xEA. * IT REFUTED ITS OWN LEADING HYPOTHESIS rather than resting on it: 'the drive does not advertise FLUSH CACHE' was tested with TWO discriminating IDENTIFY variants (word 83=0x5000 and 0x7000). The guest DEMONSTRABLY READ the new IDENTIFY -- it began issuing 0xEF SET FEATURES, which it never did before -- and STILL never flushed. Why OpenBSD declines is an honest UNKNOWN: there is no OpenBSD source in this tree, and reconstructing wd_flushcache from memory is exactly the trap the SH-manual rule exists to prevent. * *** THE LIVE DEFECT IS THE ARM, NOT THE OPCODE: 0xE0 STANDBY IMMEDIATE hits the same default: on EVERY `halt -p`, measured 4 of 4 shutdown runs. *** ABRT to the guest, no interrupt, unlatched host warning, and the guest swallows it silently. So the IDE side has a reachable reproducible fall-through TODAY, and FLUSH CACHE is an unreached member of the same set. * THE FIX IS NOT A ONE-LINER. diskimage_sync() takes a struct diskimage *, but dev_wdc.c only ever holds (machine, id, type) -- and THERE IS NO EXPORTED (machine,id,type) -> struct lookup; every public function in diskimage.c open-codes the same 6-line walk. Needs a diskimage_sync_id() wrapper, a WDCC_FLUSHCACHE_EXT constant, and a case arm that also sets int_assert. Built privately: 0xE7/0xEA become err=0x00 irq=1 fatal=0 with trace F(data) S(data), matching the SCSI sibling. * DETECTOR BUILT, and it COMPILES AGAINST BOTH TREES because the rows pass a RAW OPCODE INTEGER rather than the WDCC_ constant -- deliberately sidestepping the exact trap diff_diskimage_sync.c's header records, where naming the new symbol made the pre-fix arm a SETUP result. 9 rows / 0 failed pre-fix; 8 of 9 flip post-fix. Needs only two extra stubs given the flags gate_offline.sh already passes. * SCOPE: all three files are byte-identical between est/ and GXEMUL-SEC/. And wdc is far from landisk-only -- bus_isa, bus_pci, dev_pcic, dev_ps2_spd, machine_arc.c:235, machine_landisk.c:87 and promemul/of.c all instantiate it, so ARC IS A SECOND ATA RIG THAT WAS NOT TESTED. Words 82-87 -- the COMMAND SET SUPPORTED / ENABLED block -- are left ZERO by the opening memset. A device that advertises no command sets and aborts a command it never claimed is not obviously wrong. On that reading idesync is a MISSING FEATURE, not a durability defect, and the 'correct' fix is a much larger IDENTIFY change that collides with diff_wdc_identify.c's explicit frozen-scope banner (#405/#407/#408/#410/#411). The negative control is stronger than claimed and still does not rescue the row: word 83 = 0x5000/0x7000 sets the validity marker plus the flush bits, the guest demonstrably read the new block, and it STILL never flushed. With words 82, 85 and 86 zero the block is internally inconsistent, which is a plausible reason a driver would decline -- but that is a HYPOTHESIS, and 'why OpenBSD declines' remains an honest UNKNOWN. The wrapper claim is CHECKED TRUE: diskimage.c open-codes the machine->first_diskimage walk TWELVE times (:113, 321, 340, 360, 385, 1558, 2120, 2130, 2149, 2177, 2198, 2310); a diskimage_sync_id() would be the thirteenth. Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** LIVE VIA TWO OPCODES IN TWO ARMS, NOT ONE -- AND THE SECOND ARM IS ABSENT FROM THIS ROW. *** dev_wdc.c:572-579, the 'Unsupported commands, without warning' group, sets WDCE_ABRT and returns with NO interrupt and NO log: measured 0xF5 -> err=0x04, irq=0, fatal=0. *** AND 0xF5 SEC_FREEZE_LOCK IS ISSUED ON A PLAIN LANDISK BOOT WITH A DISK *** -- no halt, no install. So the row is reachable at rung 4 today. Credit where it belongs: agy, grok and kimi EACH found this arm from the packet; this seat confirmed it by execution and supplied the boot witness. The ledger did not contain it -- see [[ledgerboiler]] for why, which is the more important finding. BLAST RADIUS, which no seat had quantified: int_assert is a LEVEL, not an edge. dev_wdc_tick() re-asserts on EVERY tick while it is set and only a STATUS read clears it (:999-1000). Measured: HELD-LINE 0xe0 (abort), shipping : 0 asserts over 1000 ticks HELD-LINE 0x10 RECAL, shipping : 1001 asserts over 1000 ticks after ONE status read, 1000 more: +0 asserts, 1 deassert HELD-LINE 0xe0 (abort), POST-FIX : 1001 asserts over 1000 ticks <-- 0 -> 1001 *** NOT A NEW CLASS: *** RECAL already behaves exactly this way for every implemented opcode today, and the deassert is clean. Exposure is a guest that issues an unimplemented opcode fire-and-forget and never reads status. BLANKET IS RIGHT, and the file settles it without an ATA spec (there is none in this tree -- _scratchpad/ has ARM, IDT, MC88100, MIPS only, so no page numbers may be cited). There are FIVE WDCE_ABRT sites and THREE ALREADY ASSERT: :465-466 (no disk image), :473-474 (CDROM IDENTIFY), :514/:517 (SET_FEATURES unknown subcommand -- measured 0xEF -> err=0x04, irq=3). Only :578 and :582 do not. Opcode-specific gating is what CREATED the inconsistency. IMPLEMENTATION TRAP: WDCC_STANDBY_IMMED (wdcreg.h:138) and ATAPI_STANDBY_IMMEDIATE (:206) are BOTH 0xe0 -- writing both case labels is a duplicate-case compile error. SEVERITY, honestly: measured harm today is NIL. Zero unimplemented-command warnings on a disk boot, OpenBSD swallows the 0xF5 abort and reaches the prompt, and halt -p stops the machine anyway. This is fidelity for guests we do not have. — evidence: /tmp/opuswdc/probe.c dual-oracle harness; landisk boot with -d iR:·······

Final review (flagship adjudication)·✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — *** THE '10 REAL OPCODES' FIGURE IS MEASURED FALSE, AND THE CORRECTION REMOVES THIS ROW'S STATED VALUE. *** Booted with the exact rig args plus a disk: 14 command-register writes across SEVEN opcodes to the installer prompt -- 3x 0xEC IDENTIFY 3x 0x20 READ 2x 0xC6 SETMULTI 2x 0x91 IDP 2x 0x10 RECAL 1x 0xF5 SEC_FREEZE_LOCK 1x 0xC4 READMULTI "Unimplemented command" warnings: 0 No 0xE0, no 0x30 WRITE, no 0xC5 WRITEMULTI -- those come from a full filesystem lifecycle through halt -p, which this rig never performs. Grok predicted this from reading; it is now measured. *** CONSEQUENCE: adding -d i: gives ZERO coverage of the default: arm -- the arm all four defect rows live in. *** Its real value is as [[wdcnoirq]]'s rung-4 witness via 0xF5, which is a different and smaller claim. SAFE TO ADD -- measured, fixed 25 s windows, same host and binary: no disk prompt_reached=1 instrs=2,852,727,965 iR: 64MB blank prompt_reached=1 instrs=1,879,394,907 no disk (2) prompt_reached=1 instrs=2,382,496,189 iR: 64MB (2) prompt_reached=1 instrs=1,711,379,982 Both reach the installer menu; wd0 attaches and is probed; gate_crossfamily.sh's SH7751R,42 token is unaffected; the installer waits rather than auto-installing. *** TWO TRAPS. (1) SYNTAX: `-d i:R:<path>` ABORTS *** (diskimage_add(): invalid prefix char -- the parser at diskimage.c:1700-1755 takes all prefix chars before a SINGLE colon). The correct form is `-d iR:<path>`. Getting this wrong is exactly the 'latently red for two commits' shape. *** (2) THE DISK CONFIG RETIRES 28-34% FEWER INSTRUCTIONS IN THE SAME WALL TIME. *** Harmless today only because drive_guest.py:84 sets "budget": 0 -- landisk deliberately has no instruction ceiling. But its own comment says a NINSTRS floor is FILED, and *** a floor derived from today's diskless boot and applied to a disked one is a false-FAIL waiting to happen. *** Also: the base image must be R:-prefixed or the guest writes the shared rig image, and the installer prompt has NO TRAILING NEWLINE, which is why the rig needs drive_guest.py's pty predicate rather than line-oriented matching. — evidence: landisk boots with and without -d iR:, 4 fixed-window runs·······

It also rejected the ledger's own grouping argument ('both fixes are a dozen lines together') as a SIZE argument, which is not one of the prongs. Separately it found that `timeout=` as I specified it is not enough for the BUILD phase, and that `start_new_session` is what makes killpg safe -- without it the children share the GATE's process group and killpg is gate suicide. Its stated MECHANISM (a blocking post-kill drain) was measured FALSE on POSIX; the conclusion held for a different reason. — evidence: _scratchpad/panel_20260819_232621/✓2026-08-19 — CONFIRMED — DERIVED THE TIMEOUTS FROM MEASUREMENT rather than choosing them: slowest build across all 12 lanes 1.37 s, slowest run 0.31 s, on an idle machine. Recommends build=120 s (~88x) and run=60 s (~190x), SEPARATE, env-overridable -- separate because the diagnoses differ (a two-minute compile means the host is sick; a spinning run is the EXPECTED mutant outcome) and because the SETUP message must name the phase. On margin it cited this project's own gate_ab, which uses 3x and measurably false-FAILed a 45-minute battery under load, so 3x is KNOWN-INSUFFICIENT here. It measured the process-group kill both ways: run(timeout=) returned at 3.00 s and left the spinner alive; Popen(start_new_session)+killpg reaped the whole tree, child pgid 32 against the gate's 11, so killpg provably cannot reach the gate. The file's own header carries the author's TODO at line 35: '(Split counter[] into reset value and current value.)' So d->counter[] is the PROGRAMMED RELOAD VALUE, FROZEN. gxemul models the timer's RATE (timer_add / timer_update_frequency) and its INTERRUPTS, but never a counting register. WHY THAT REFRAMES THE FIX: OpenBSD's microtime() latches and reads the counter to INTERPOLATE SUB-TICK TIME. If a 'correct' latch returns a constant, the guest's interpolated time does not advance within a tick -- a different wrong answer from 0, and arguably a WORSE one because it is plausible rather than obviously broken. So the candidate that looks most correct (return the programmed value) may be the one that misleads a guest furthest, and the honest round may be smaller than the row implies: make the latch not-an-error and not-a-flood, and DOCUMENT that sub-tick interpolation is unmodelled. Here a latch write CLOBBERS mode_byte (destroying the RW format the guest set earlier) and ZEROES d->mode[counter], because the latch command's mode bits are 0. SO EVEN A GUEST THAT NEVER READS THE LATCHED VALUE HAS HAD ITS COUNTER SILENTLY REPROGRAMMED. That is a distinct consequence from pitlatch's (a latch-then-read returns 0 and floods the host log): this one damages state on the WRITE alone. Reachability inherits pitlatch's: OpenBSD's microtime() issues the latch command (_guest-src-openbsd22/sys/arch/i386/isa/clock.c:207-209), so the clobber happens on every call. NOT MEASURED -- no probe has yet shown the downstream effect of the corrupted RW format, and the honest grade is READ until one does. The residual it named is now row hlen; it must not be filed under this refuted claim.closed

Either reason alone is fatal. (2) THE '~7.9 s FOR FOUR TIMERS' FIGURE: confirmed impossible, and the seat found WHERE THE NUMBER CAME FROM, which is better than refuting it. 2^31 / (4 x 1048576 x 65) = 7.876 s -- the single-element floor divided by four. The counters are per-timer (:73), each callback increments its own element (:86-92), and the catch-up budget is per-timer too (timer.c:281, inside the per-timer loop), so four timers overflow four DIFFERENT elements at their own rates. True floors: 42.950 s cats (2^31/50,000,000, machine_cats.c:56-57) now measured three times at 43.03/43.10/44.58, and 33.686 s netwinder (2^31/63,750,000, machine_netwinder.c:56). ONE REFINEMENT worth recording: a hard floor of 31.51 s exists from the catch-up ceiling (2^31/68,157,440), but it needs a timer at or above 68.16 MHz, which neither machine's emulated_hz permits. cats's is guarded by `if (== 0)` so a config-file emulated_hz word could reach it; netwinder's is unconditional. Research (fix proposals)·…2026-08-19 — BUILT AND CLOSED, and it IMPROVED ON THE RECIPE IT WAS GIVEN. Told to build the single-overlay row a prior pass had specified, it built that, then probed two SIBLING mutants and measured that the single-overlay row catches ONLY the deletion: `continue` -> `break;` and `continue` -> `return 0;` both pass it GREEN, because with one overlay there is no next iteration and all three mutants trace identically. A SECOND OVERLAY separates them and one row kills all three. It supplied both patches and recommended the stronger, which also perturbs no existing gate check where the fallback would have forced one from "1" to "2". * Mechanism: __wrap_fsync consults a static fail_fsync_fd, sets errno=EIO and returns -1 without calling __real_fsync; armed after the WRITE, disarmed when the command returns. It rejected, with reasons written into the file, a real failing fsync (needs dm-error/root, non-portable -- same class as the drvfs trap), close()ing the fd under the live FILE* (a FAULT, and can hit a recycled fd) and an O_RDONLY fd (rc 0 on glibc, proves nothing). * A CRASH IS NOT WHAT MAKES IT FAIL, measured four ways: rc is 1 never >=128; the mutant printed all 11 rows plus the verdict line so it reached the end of main; ASan+UBSan produced 0 bytes on both arms; and exactly one row differs, by a printed string. * INSTRUMENT-SABOTAGE CONTROL (`if (0 && fd == fail_fsync_fd)`) turns TWO rows red, so a dead injection fails loudly and the signatures are distinguishable: two red together = the instrument, the ordering row red alone = the code. * VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE MAIN LOOP, and MY FIRST THREE ATTEMPTS WERE ALL VOID -- the loop variable was eaten before reaching WSL and the printed rc was grep's status; then the anchor took 'the first continue in a range' when the loop has TWO and the f_data==NULL branch never executes, so all three mutants 'passed' and would have discredited the row; then anchoring on the fsync call matched :1211 in overlay_set_block_in_use, a different function. Only a context printout of the line about to be mutated caught it. Correctly anchored on the unique 'Data is not durable' comment: ALL THREE MUTANTS KILLED, traces distinguishable -- deleted publishes b0 anyway, break/return0 stop at F(d0) S(d0). * Gate 2: PASS 235 checks (was 231). Honest limits recorded in the file: the CHECK-CONDITION row is a WITNESS not a discriminator (green on every code mutant); an fflush failure on the data file is not injected, only fsync; and the injection skips the real fsync, so a partially-successful sync is UNTESTED and UNKNOWN. The carrier is explicit that conflating them is how a two-seat review gets reported as a panel, so the round closes naming the omission rather than over the top of it.✓2026-08-20 — CONFIRMED — MEASURED at rung 3. dev_8253.c:170-171 CLEARS I8253_TIMER_LSB and nothing ever sets it back; a real 8254's flip-flop ALTERNATES on every access. Two full LSB/MSB pairs after one mode write produced THREE recomputes -- 97 Hz, **0 Hz**, 97 Hz -- where hardware does two. TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the first is what makes it matter: it transiently drives the counter to ZERO, i.e. straight into the i8253zero defect, FROM A GUEST THAT NEVER PROGRAMS COUNT 0. That inverts the reachability finding on i8253zero, where no available guest asks for count 0 directly. Second: if the second pair's LSB is nonzero it is SILENTLY LOST -- intending 0x3055 the device holds 0x3000. FOR: UB in a signal handler; exit() runs atexit and _IO_cleanup, taking stdio locks the interrupted main thread may hold; a hang is a strictly worse failure shape than an exit. AGAINST, measured: the seat built the exact two calls and fired them from a 65 Hz SIGALRM (timer.c's own rate) into a main thread saturated with stdio, then into one saturated with malloc/free carrying an ALLOCATING atexit handler: CONTROL (main thread) exit rc=1, message intact SIGALRM, stdio 10/10 exited rc=1, message intact, 0/10 hung SIGALRM, malloc 12/12 exited rc=1, atexit ran, 0/12 hung GXemul registers exactly ONE atexit handler (fix_console, emul.c:913), so the realistic exit path is short. A negative result on one glibc -- but it is the platform this project builds and gates on, and 22 trials produced zero difference. *** AND THE OTHER HALF DOES NOT RESCUE THE ROW. *** The 'a legal guest write kills the host' reframing looked like a missed #223 instance until the seat COUNTED: grep -c 'exit(1)' src/devices/*.c finds 50 FILES, and dev_sh4.c carries no #223 tag at all. This is not one path a completed sweep missed (the wdcflood shape); it is one member of a large untouched class, and picking it because a timer row happened to notice it is the wrong selection criterion. FALSE. The spy is a TWO-DIRECTIONAL presence oracle -- rows assert zero purges where none is owed AND non-zero where one IS owed, and the second group reddens the instant the callback stops being called. There is no in-file mutant satisfying 'purge achieved, spy silent, rows green', because THE CALLBACK IS THE MECHANISM. The seat's own negative control is why this is believable: its first mutant silently no-op'd (python3 in git-bash is the Microsoft Store stub) and the harness printed a clean 27/0 PASS. A cmp against the pristine copy caught it and that run was discarded. Rule 4 -- 'did it fail for the reason under test' -- earning its keep again. — evidence: diff_m8invread.c mutant D1, built and run·······

The probe reported PRE_FIX_SYMPTOM rather than a confusing failure, which is a detector giving a legible answer when its input is wrong. * THE THIRD TIME THIS GATE WENT RED FOR THIS REASON, and the second was ONE COMMIT EARLIER THE SAME DAY: the footbridge probe had the identical coupling, a subagent warned about it, it was handled correctly, the annotation recording the lesson was written -- and then the same mistake was made with a different probe. This row exists because of that finding. * Q1 THE WITNESS IS GENUINELY RUNG 3, all three clauses, no laundering: committed rig image under R:, no device_add, no new machine; every planted word disassembled and text-compared before stepping, with an encoding mismatch exiting as SETUP rather than passing -- the hand-assembled-encoding trap is guarded. What is forfeited is the LICENSING semantics -- the reproduction was meant to license the edit and instead verified it retroactively. * TWO HARDENING NITS: the PRE_FIX_SYMPTOM verdict does not require C2 to have PASSED, so 'died for the right reason' is enforced by transcript reading rather than by the token -- one `if fails:` guard makes it self-guarding. The program gen_dashboard.py makes this page from pipeline/ledger.json. Do not change this page manually. If a cell does not have a ledger entry, the cell is a defect. A packet-fed seat examines the argument only. Its vote about the contents of the repository is not equal to the vote of a seat that reads files (PIPELINE.md, Section 1). An ✕ cell can be the most important cell in its row: the ✕ in the Research phase of #419 changed the design. Rule for closed rows (owner, 2026-08-15): a closed row does not need new tests when the flagship seat (Fable) examined the final change and its evidence. That examination fills the Final review cell of the closed row. Regression phase (owner, 2026-08-15): only the flagship seat reviews the regression tests, and the reviews are BATCHED TO SUNDAY NIGHT, after the full battery, which now runs Sunday at 18:00 so that its evidence covers the rounds the review examines. The other eight cells in a Regression line are NOT REQUIRED, and a Regression line that is empty on a round finished after Saturday is WAITING FOR THE SUNDAY BATCH, not missing. So a line of dots there shows a rule, not a gap. The first three phases still need all nine seats, per round, before that round proceeds.
